title: Insight 1: Nov 1 ride breached easy ceiling by ~19 bpm
description: On Nov 1, your max HR hit 195 bpm, well above your lactate threshold (175 bpm). For a joyful rider, keep easy days truly easy — aim to stay under 159 bpm (Z2 ceiling) on recovery rides.

title: Insight 2: Nov 12 long ride vertical load high at 506m over 50km
description: The Nov 12 ride packed 506 m of climbing into 50 km (10 m/km), the steepest density in your recent block. That's fine for fun, but if legs feel heavy next day, consider a flatter route for the next long ride.

title: Insight 3: Back-to-back rides Nov 5–6 flag recovery sequencing risk
description: You rode on consecutive days Nov 5 (50 km) and Nov 6 (47 km) with only ~22 h between finishes. For happiness riding, insert a rest or easy spin day after two-day blocks to keep freshness high.

title: Insight 4: Cycling progression — VO2max up to 50, 20-min power 224 W
description: Your cycling VO2max has nudged from 49 to 50 since late Oct, and your best 20-min power (224 W on Nov 12) suggests FTP around 213 W. That's a solid, gradual gain — keep enjoying the process.

title: Insight 5: Zone model check — HR and power zones align reasonably
description: Your HR Z2 (139–159 bpm) matches power Z2 (117–160 W) well for your current FTP (213 W) and LTHR (175 bpm). No urgent need to retest, but a fresh 20-min effort would tighten both.

title: Insight 6: Polarized 80/20 — most ride time in Z2, few hard efforts
description: Average HRs (135–158 bpm) show >80% of recent ride time in Z1–Z2, with only brief spikes above threshold. That's a healthy polarised split for a happiness rider — no change needed.

title: Insight 7: Recovery signs — readiness rising but last 3 days missing
description: Readiness climbed from 67 to 77 between Nov 11–14, HRV 57→71, RHR 54→50. However, no wellness data for Nov 15–17; if you feel tired, trust the gap and take an easy day.

title: Insight 8: Strength — maximal power shows sprint potential (981 W 10s)
description: Your 10-sec peak hit 981 W (Nov 5) and 579 W (Nov 8), indicating good neuromuscular pop. One weekly hill sprint or gym session can maintain this reactive strength without fatigue.

title: Insight 9: VO2max booster — add 4×4 min at 230–240 W once a week
description: To nudge VO2max above 50, try a simple set: 4 × 4 min at ~110% FTP (230–240 W) with 4 min easy spin, on a fresh day. Keep it playful — stop if it feels like a chore.

title: Insight 10: FTP suggestion — update from 213 W using recent 20-min best
description: Your current FTP estimate (213 W) comes from 95% of 224 W (Nov 12). A dedicated 20-min test or a hard 30-min group ride would give a fresher number and sharpen zone targets.
